title: Company-wide policies and processes (Consolidated)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:
This consolidated policy document provides Redwood Inference's company-wide standards and procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management & retention, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. These policies aim to balance security, operational velocity, and cost control while providing clear ownership and escalation paths.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems or data.
- Teams must maintain service-specific standards (runbooks, access matrices) and link them from this page.

Table of contents:
1) Principles and responsibilities
2) Access & permissions
3) Change management
4) Data management and retention
5) Procurement & expenses
6) Vendor management and vendor security reviews
7) Travel policy
8) Internal templates and request forms
9) Versioning and review cadence

1) Principles and responsibilities
- Least privilege: provide minimum necessary access; approvals must be evidence-based with defined expiration.
- Visible, reversible changes: changes that affect production must be scheduled, documented, and have a rollback path.
- Protect and minimize data: classify, protect, and retain data only as required by law or contract.
- Ownership: People Ops maintains this document. Security owns access controls and vendor security reviews. Finance & Legal own procurement terms. SRE and Platform own change and backup runbooks.
- Escalation: Report policy violations or exceptions to the policy owner and security@redwood.example for triage.

2) Access & permissions
Access model:
- RBAC: Centralized role-based access control via the company IdP and group management.
- Temporary elevation: All temporary admin privileges must be requested via the access-request template with justification, owner, and expiration date (max 72 hours for break-glass access).
Provisioning flow:
1. New hire/contractor: Manager completes onboarding request; People Ops creates HR record and triggers IdP provisioning; service owners grant service-level access.
2. Service-level access: Service owners maintain an access matrix and approve requests for their service.
Approval thresholds:
- Standard access: Manager approval.
- Production or sensitive data access: Manager + Security reviewer.
- Finance system access: Manager + Finance approver.
Offboarding:
- Deprovisioning: Execute offboard checklist within 4 business hours for contractors and within 24 hours for standard departures. Automated deprovisioning should be used where integrated with HR/IdP.
Auditing:
- Quarterly access reviews for any group with production or confidential data privileges; owners must attest in writing.
Exceptions/Break-glass:
- JIT emergency access workflow must be used; all emergency sessions must be logged and a post-mortem submitted within 3 business days.

3) Change management
Change categories:
- Standard changes: Pre-authorized, repeatable operational activities with documented rollback.
- Minor changes: Low-risk changes requiring owner approval and logging.
- Major changes: High-impact changes (schema migrations, infra changes, deploys to critical services) requiring CAB review.
- Emergency changes: Changes required to restore service; document and retroactively review with CAB.
CAB (Change Advisory Board):
- Membership: SRE lead, Platform engineering, Security, Product operations, and a rotating engineering representative.
- Cadence: Meets twice weekly; ad-hoc for urgent approvals.
Deployment windows and blackout periods:
- Standard deployment window: Weekdays 10:00-18:00 local region.
- Blackout windows: End-of-quarter customer-facing release windows and other service-specific blackout periods.
Change request requirements:
- Must include: summary, owner, impact assessment, rollback plan, test plan, monitoring runbook (metrics/logs), scheduled window, stakeholders, and approvals.
Rollback & verification:
- Major changes should include automated rollback where feasible and a verification checklist tied to SLO metrics.

4) Data management and retention
Classification:
- Public: Information approved for public disclosure.
- Internal: Default classification for non-sensitive internal information.
- Confidential: Customer PII, credentials, billing details, and contractually protected data.
Handling requirements:
- Confidential data must be stored encrypted at rest and in transit; access limited to approved groups with logged access.
- Secrets must live in the approved secret store (KMS/HSM); secrets are prohibited in code, repos, or plaintext documents.
Retention and deletion:
- Logs: Default retention 90 days; shorter windows encouraged for high-volume debug logs.
- Customer PII: Retention per contract and law; default retention 2 years unless specified.
- Data subject requests: Route to privacy@redwood.example; respond within 30 days.
Backups and resilience:
- Backup SLAs: Critical services target RPO 24 hours and prioritized systems RTO 4 hours. Monthly backup verification sampling required.
Monitoring and alerts:
- Automated detection for bulk exports or anomalous access with alerts to Security and service owners.

5) Procurement & expenses
Procurement flow:
1. Purchases <$5,000: Manager approval via procurement request template.
2. Purchases $5,000-$50,000: Manager + Finance approver.
3. Purchases >$50,000: Manager + Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor.
Recurrent subscriptions:
- Renewals >$10,000/year must be reviewed by Finance & Legal prior to renewal. Centralize subscriptions where practical.
Expense reimbursement:
- Submit expenses with receipts and a business purpose within 30 days using the expense report template. Exceptions require manager + Finance approval.
Preferred vendors:
- Use the approved vendor list; for new vendor onboarding follow vendor checklist and security review.

6) Vendor management and security reviews
Onboarding checklist:
- Confirm business need and owner.
- Legal: NDA and contract terms executed.
- Finance: Billing model and KYC completed.
- Security: Complete vendor questionnaire, request SOC 2/ISO evidence where applicable, and document data handling obligations.
Security review tiers:
- Tier 1 (low risk): SaaS with no access to customer data; questionnaire + owner approval.
- Tier 2 (medium risk): Tools accessing internal systems or non-PII data; documentation review and security follow-up required.
- Tier 3 (high risk): Tools that store/process customer PII or participate in production path; require SOC 2/ISO evidence, penetration test results (if available), contract data clauses, and Security + Legal approval.
SLA & monitoring:
- Vendor owner must define availability SLAs and incident communication cadence; include escalation contacts in contract.
Renewal and offboarding:
- Start renewals >$10k/year at least 90 days prior. Offboarding must include data deletion/return confirmation and credential revocation within 48 hours.

7) Travel policy
Booking & approval:
- Manager pre-approval required using travel request template with purpose and estimated cost.
- Use preferred travel vendor/tool unless an exception is granted.
Allowable expenses:
- Lodging: Reasonable single-occupancy rate per corporate rate card.
- Meals: Per-diem by location; receipts required.
- Air travel: Economy for flights under 6 hours. Business class requires Director-level approval or documented exception.
Safety & insurance:
- Employees traveling to high-risk locations must enroll in People Ops travel advisory and obtain insurance if not centrally provided.
Reimbursement:
- Submit expenses within 30 days; unapproved expenditures may be denied.

8) Internal templates and request forms
- Onboarding request: /confluence/templates/onboarding-request
- Access request: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change request: /confluence/templates/change-request
- Procurement request: /confluence/templates/procurement-request
- Expense report: /confluence/templates/expense-report
- Vendor onboarding checklist: /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding
- Travel request: /confluence/templates/travel-request
- Incident post-mortem: /confluence/templates/incident-postmortem

9) Versioning and review cadence
- Ownership: People Ops owns this document and will conduct an annual review. Security and Finance will review vendor and procurement sections bi-annually or sooner if regulatory or business needs change.
- Change log:
  - 2025-01-15: Initial consolidated policy created.
  - 2025-09-01: JIT emergency access procedure and backup RTO updates added.
  - 2026-03-01: Procurement thresholds and vendor tiers updated.
  - 2026-03-04: Minor clarifications to approval thresholds and offboarding timelines.

Appendices:
- Owners: People Ops (policy maintainer), Security (access & vendor reviews), Finance & Legal (procurement & contracts), SRE/Platform (change management & backups), Managers (local approvals).
- Contacts: people-ops@redwood.example, security@redwood.example, procurement@redwood.example, finance@redwood.example, privacy@redwood.example.

Exceptions process:
1. Complete the exception request template with justification, compensating controls, and expected duration.
2. Submit to People Ops and cc security@redwood.example.
3. Exceptions >90 days require Exec approval and quarterly attestation by the service owner.
